topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecturer, the cancer lecture series, and the core learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Endogenous Factors, Environment, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the conceptual framework of cancer development as an evolutionary process driven by an interplay between intrinsic cellular errors, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological variations.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens and Burkitt Lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how biological agents drive oncogenesis, using the relationship between Epstein-Barr virus, malaria, and Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Carcinogens and DNA Damage Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore specific chemical mutagens and radiation that induce mutations either directly or via metabolic activation into reactive DNA-damaging intermediates.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Cell Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address non-mutagenic contributions to cancer development, focusing on promotional signaling cascades, inflammatory microenvironments, and developmental stages of cellular vulnerability.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying Carcinogens and Assessing Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the mutational signature analyses, epidemiological tools, and laboratory assays used to determine carcinogenicity and evaluate cancer risk.
